note: Word count bands for pages the handbook's page type band does not fit. Applied by tools/architecture.py when a brief is generated, after the tier scaling in decision 002. A declared list, not a heuristic: nothing mechanical separates a narrow structure from a narrow description of a wide one. An entry is a prediction about a page that is not yet written, so it is checked once the page exists and withdrawn if it was wrong. Withdrawn entries are kept below rather than deleted, because the wrong prediction is the useful part of the record.

2.10.6.title: Common Peroneal Nerve
2.10.6.reason: The client asked on 9 October 2026 for a section on the nerve at risk from lateral surgery, and decision 013 gave the page a fellowship tier to carry it. That tier is a single Clinical Relevance section of ten paragraphs, which is the deliverable rather than padding around one. The handbook's 800 to 1800 band is written for an anatomy page with the usual four or five body sections per tier, and this page has four tiers and an eleventh section on top.
2.10.6.checked: Written at 2227 words. The override is a prediction like every other entry here, and it was right: the page came in inside the band without prose being added to fill it.

2.2.3.title: Tibial Spine
2.2.3.reason: A single bony eminence. Its attachments are the cruciate and meniscal roots, which 2.5, 2.6, 2.7 and 2.8 own, and tibial spine avulsion is pathology owned by 6.101 and 10.35.
2.2.3.withdrawn: Predicted narrow before the page was written. It came out at 1219 words of substantive anatomy, not padding, so the prediction was wrong and the override was withdrawn rather than the prose cut. The handbook's own 800 to 1800 band applies.

assessment: All six narrow structure predictions were wrong and all six have been withdrawn: 2.2.3, 2.2.4, 2.3.1, 2.3.2, 2.3.3 and 2.4.2. Not one of them came in under 1100 words. The idea did not work, and the reason is now clear: page length follows from how many relations a structure has, not from how small the structure is. Gerdy's tubercle is one bump with a disputed ligament on it; the proximal fibula is a small bone with a major nerve lying on it. Both need as many words as a femoral condyle. The handbook's 800 to 1800 band was right and the prediction method was not. No override is active, and none should be declared for a page that has not been written. See decision 005.
